name: Bronzebeard clan
summary: In Ironforge, King Magni Bronzebeard leads his clan and its kingdom. The Bronzebeards won the War of the Three Hammers, then forged close ties with humanity and the gnomes. Now they anchor the Alliance.

sections.title: The War of the Three Hammers
sections.body:
High King Modimus Anvilmar’s death opened old rivalries within Ironforge. For years, dwarven society had flourished under his rule, but when he died of old age about two hundred and thirty years ago, those rivalries became civil war. Thane Madoran Bronzebeard commanded Ironforge’s traditional garrison and largest standing army. He drove the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans from beneath the mountain.

Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan attacked to reclaim Khaz Modan, and Madoran led his clan and army in a decisive campaign. The Bronzebeards shattered the Dark Iron host and secured their supremacy over Ironforge.

sections.title: A Pillar of the Alliance
sections.body:
The Bronzebeards and human kingdoms first met nearly two thousand years ago. Their shared skill in metalcraft, trade, and battle built mutual respect. Then the Orcish Horde swept across the continent in the Second War, and King Magni Bronzebeard brought his realm into the Alliance of Lordaeron.

The Bronzebeards withstood brutal sieges inside their subterranean fortress. Their engineers, gunners, and demolitionists supplied vital firepower and arms, helping turn the tide of war.

sections.title: Grief at the High Seat
sections.body:
King Magni Bronzebeard governs from the High Seat in the Great Forge. His younger brother, Muradin Bronzebeard, served as an Alliance emissary in Lordaeron before vanishing in Northrend’s frozen wastes alongside Prince Arthas Menethil. Muradin was presumed dead when the prince claimed Frostmourne, the cursed blade.

Magni’s daughter, Princess Moira, has also gone missing. With the succession uncertain, the clan searches ancient Titan excavation sites to divine its origins.

faq.answer: King Magni Bronzebeard rules the clan from the High Seat in the Great Forge. A veteran of the Second War and a master smith, he leads his clan and the allied dwarves of Khaz Modan.

faq.q: How did the Bronzebeard clan win control of Ironforge?
faq.answer: The Bronzebeards won control of Ironforge in the civil war that followed High King Modimus Anvilmar’s death about two hundred and thirty years ago. Thane Madoran Bronzebeard commanded Ironforge’s central standing army and drove the Wildhammers and Dark Irons from the mountain. Then he led his clan and army to crush Thaurissan’s invading Dark Iron force.

faq.q: What is the difference between Bronzebeard and other dwarven clans?
faq.answer: The Bronzebeards inhabit Ironforge and represent the traditional mountain dwarves, known for heavy plate, firearms, and subterranean architecture. The Wildhammers dwell among the crags and skies as gryphon riders, while the hostile Dark Irons master dark sorcery and pyromancy beneath Blackrock Mountain.

Muradin Bronzebeard traveled to Northrend as an Alliance emissary and explorer. He guided Prince Arthas Menethil in the hunt for Frostmourne, a runeblade, and was reported dead when the prince freed the cursed weapon from its pedestal.

faq.q: Why are the Bronzebeards so devoted to archaeological digs?
faq.answer: Bronzebeard scholars have found relics linking their ancestry to the ancient, stone-hewn earthen. Driven to discover their race’s roots, the clan funds digs and expeditions across Azeroth.

faq.q: Where is the Bronzebeard royal family's seat of power?
faq.answer: The Bronzebeard royal family’s seat of power is the High Seat, situated in the heart of Ironforge along the Great Forge. King Magni conducts state affairs there, surrounded by councilors and royal guards.

angles.text: As a dwarf, you hail from or answer to the Bronzebeard kingdom. You serve King Magni as a steadfast defender of Khaz Modan.
As a gnome, you can remember that the Bronzebeards offered refuge in Ironforge’s Tinkertown when Gnomeregan fell to the trogg invasion.
As a human, you share longstanding ties with the Bronzebeards, built through trade and shared martial traditions.
As a blacksmith, you can look to the Bronzebeards, renowned across Azeroth for their mastery of smelting, weapon crafting, and heavy armors.
